ABSTRACT 
This project addresses the growing concern of withering attention spans among 
the GCSE student demographic, likely caused by frequent usage of fast-paced 
social media platforms such as TikTok. This project attempts to resolve this 
issue, through the development of an eLearning application utilising short-form 
videos, competitive leader boards, performance-contingent rewards, and a 
variety of question types. Utilising a waterfall-agile hybrid development strategy, 
the platform has been designed to align with current learning needs and digital 
engagement strategies. Empirical data from this project indicates that despite 
increasing distractibility, the novel features introduced in this project enhanced 
student engagement and exam performance, highlighting the effectiveness of 
gamified short-form content in improving educational outcomes. Future research 
should endeavour to explore the long-term effects of short-form content in 
educational settings.
